To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the jet calculus is an efficient and powerful method to calculate the cross sections for hard jet processes in QCD; (2) the jet calculus provides a simple and elegant method to derive the parton‐based probabilistic algorithms; (3) the jet calculus allows one to study the next‐to leading corrections to the jet cross sections and to the jet probabilities.

(i) the jet cross sections can be calculated in the leading log and next‐to‐ leading log approximations; (ii) the parton distributions can be extracted from the data; (iii) the parton‐shower models are not needed; (iv) the parton distribution is not universal; (v) the next‐to leading‐log approximation is needed to resolve the jets
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a theory of hadronic jets in perturbative Qcd.
the study of jets produced in hard QCD processes.
the development of the jet calculus, a new tool for the analysis of the structure of jets produced in hard collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the leading log approximation is a good starting point, but that it is necessary to go to the next‐ to‐leading order to get a reliable quantitative picture of QCD jets.
the leading log jet calculus is a well‐defined and useful tool, which has a number of interesting and nontrivial consequences.
the jet calculus has been successfully developed, but it is still not complete.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a way to calculate the probability that a jet contains a given number of partons, in a given state, with given momenta.
the jet calculus is a very useful tool in studying QCD jets.
, with the help of jet calculus, the parton picture can be extended to a parton‐probabilities picture, in the same way the Feynman parton picture was extended to the parton‐distribution functions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the jet cross section in the leading log and next‐to‐ leading order is a sum over the cross sections of the parton‐shower configurations, each of which is weighted with a parton‐probablistic factor.
jet calculus is a very powerful tool to understand the structure of QCD jets.
, while the leading log calculation is very successful in describing the main features of the hadronic jets, it is not enough for a detailed comparison with the data.
